- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model underestimates; add 2–3% to forecast to account for risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.25) and price is trending upward, model lags; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend.
- If sentiment is flat and price is trending downward, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature reversal.
- In high volatility periods (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days with >10% price swings), model overfits short-term noise; use 10-day EWMA instead of 30-day forecast for smoothing.
